newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bond traders ponder fate of OLO 15.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bond traders ponder fate of OLO 15.

text.p: Belgian bond traders are pondering the fate of the 6.75 percent OLO 15 as time runs out for the Treasury to exchange it into longer-dated paper.
OLO 15 has been offered regularly in exchange auctions in the past months, but there remains around 98.3 billion Belgian francs outstanding of the issue, according to the Treasury.

With the bond featuring in just one more exchange auction before it matures on May 25, dealers wonder whether the Treasury plans to repay most of the issue, as well as the final 6.6 billion francs in coupons. "It's not much. They can probably afford it," one commented.
At Tuesday's auction the Treasury succeeded in persuading investors to switch 18.6 billion francs worth of the issue into longer-dated paper, mainly the 10-year benchmark OLO 26.

The Treasury plans three more exchange auctions before May 27 -- on April 15, May 13 and May 20 -- but OLO 15 only features in the May 13 auction; by contrast the 9.25 percent, January 1998, OLO 4 is on offer at all three.

Dealers said it was too early to speculate on whether the large amount outstanding in OLO 15 might signal a give-away price at the May 13 auction. Even if a good price were set on the day, the market could turn the wrong way, they noted.
Meanwhile, the focus was returning to the regular monthly OLO auction set for April 21. Primary dealers are due to hold their regular meeting with the Treasury before the auction on Monday.

It will be the last meeting of the present circle of primary dealers before the statute of primary dealers is theoretically "liberalised" on May 1, to bring it in line with European Union directives on financial services.
A senior Treasury official reiterated on Thursday, however, it has no plans to change or modify the present composition of the primary dealers and Monday's meeting will not be the last.
